evals.name: knows where Copilot session log files live
evals.prompt: I want to find all GitHub Copilot session log files on a Linux developer machine so I can analyze token usage. Which file paths and file formats should I look at? Cover VS Code Chat, Copilot CLI, JetBrains, Gemini CLI, and Antigravity sessions.
evals.expected_output: The response lists workspaceStorage chatSessions .json files under the VS Code user directory, ~/.copilot/session-state/*.jsonl for Copilot CLI, ~/.copilot/jb/{conversationId}/partition-{n}.jsonl for JetBrains, ~/.gemini/tmp/{project}/chats/session-*.jsonl for Gemini CLI, and the Antigravity transcript.jsonl under ~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/, distinguishing .json (VS Code Chat) from .jsonl (CLI/agent) formats.
assertions: The output mentions VS Code Chat session .json files under workspaceStorage (chatSessions) in the VS Code user data directory.
The output identifies ~/.copilot/session-state/ as the location of Copilot CLI .jsonl sessions.
The output identifies ~/.copilot/jb/ as the location of JetBrains Copilot session partition .jsonl files.
The output identifies a Gemini CLI session location under ~/.gemini/tmp/ with session .jsonl files.
The output distinguishes the .json format (VS Code Copilot Chat) from the .jsonl format (CLI/agent style, one JSON event per line).

evals.name: knows the character-to-token estimation approach
evals.prompt: When a Copilot session log does not include actual token counts, how should the number of tokens be estimated from the message text, and how does the estimate account for different models?
evals.expected_output: The response describes a character-to-token ratio estimation: roughly 4 characters per token (ratio 0.25) by default, with model-specific ratios (loaded from tokenEstimators data) matched by model name, computed as ceil(text length × tokens-per-char).
assertions: The output describes estimating tokens from character counts using a characters-per-token ratio, with a default of about 4 characters per token (0.25 tokens per character).
The output states that model-specific ratios are used when the model name matches a configured estimator entry.
